concepts.title: Colored operad
concepts.description: A collection of operations with specified input and output types, with associative substitution into inputs and identity operations.

concepts.title: Connes fusion of Hilbert bimodules
concepts.description: The relative tensor product of an M–N and an N–P Hilbert bimodule, formed using bounded vectors and completion in the canonical relative inner product, producing an M–P Hilbert bimodule.

concepts.title: Hilbert bimodule over von Neumann algebras
concepts.description: An M–N Hilbert bimodule is a Hilbert space with commuting normal unital *-representations of von Neumann algebras M and Nᵒᵖ, giving left M and right N actions.

concepts.title: Hyperfinite von Neumann algebra
concepts.description: A von Neumann algebra that is the weak closure of an increasing union of finite-dimensional *-subalgebras.

concepts.title: Type II₁ factor
concepts.description: An infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra with center ℂ1 admitting a faithful normal tracial state.

concepts.title: Von Neumann dimension of a Hilbert module
concepts.description: A Hilbert module over a finite factor is represented by a projection on a sum of copies of L²(M); its dimension is the extended matrix trace of that projection.

concepts.title: Tracial L²-space of a finite von Neumann algebra
concepts.description: The Hilbert completion of M for the inner product ⟨x,y⟩=τ(y*x), with the natural left and right multiplication actions.

concepts.title: Ordered field
concepts.description: A field with a total order preserved by addition, in which the product of two positive elements is positive.

concepts.title: Absolute spectral gap of a finite Markov chain
concepts.description: For an irreducible finite transition matrix P, the absolute spectral gap is 1−max{|λ|:λ≠1 is an eigenvalue of P}. Unlike 1−λ₂ for a reversible chain, this definition allows complex eigenvalues and nonreversibility.

concepts.title: Absolutely continuous function on a real interval
concepts.description: A real function f on [a,b] is absolutely continuous if for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that any finite disjoint family of intervals (a_i,b_i) with ∑(b_i−a_i)<δ has ∑|f(b_i)−f(a_i)|<ε.

concepts.title: ANOVA decomposition on a product probability space
concepts.description: For square-integrable f(X₁,…,X_n) with independent inputs, define f_∅=Ef and f_u=E[f|X_u]−∑_{v⊊u}f_v. Then f=∑_uf_u; nonconstant components have zero conditional mean after integrating any one of their active coordinates, and distinct components are orthogonal in L².

concepts.title: Aperiodic finite Markov chain
concepts.description: A state has period equal to the gcd of its possible positive return times. An irreducible chain is aperiodic when this common period is one.

concepts.title: Discretely monitored arithmetic Asian option
concepts.description: A contingent claim whose payoff depends on an arithmetic average of asset prices at a specified finite set of monitoring times, for example (n⁻¹∑_kS_{t_k}−K)⁺.

concepts.title: Asymptotic equivalence
concepts.description: The assertion f∼g along a specified limit means f(x)/g(x)→1, where g is nonzero near that limit. Sequences are the instance x=n→∞.

concepts.title: Aubin–Lions compactness lemma
concepts.description: Let X₀↪X↪X₁ be Banach spaces, the first embedding compact and the second continuous. For1<p<∞ and1<q≤∞, a set bounded in Lᵖ(0,T;X₀) whose weak time derivatives are bounded in Lᑫ(0,T;X₁) is relatively compact in Lᵖ(0,T;X).

concepts.title: Azuma–Hoeffding inequality
concepts.description: If a real martingale has increments bounded in absolute value by c_i, then P(|M_n−M_0|≥t)≤2exp(−t²/(2∑_{i=1}^nc_i²)) for t>0.

concepts.title: b-fold coloring of a graph
concepts.description: An assignment of a set of b colors to every vertex such that adjacent vertices receive disjoint color sets. The b-fold chromatic number χ_b(G) is the smallest total number of colors permitting such an assignment.

concepts.title: Continuous dual of a normed vector space
concepts.description: The vector space X* of bounded linear maps X→its scalar field, with norm ‖ℓ‖=sup_{‖x‖≤1}|ℓ(x)|.
